question: What typically happens when the learning rate is too small or too large?
direct_answer: Too small makes training very slow; too large can overshoot minima and cause divergence or unstable oscillation.
expanded_answer: With a too-small learning rate, updates barely move the parameters, so optimization can take a very long time and may appear stuck. With a too-large learning rate, each update can jump across narrow valleys, overshoot good regions, and produce oscillation or even exploding loss. The learning rate therefore controls a stability–speed tradeoff.
key_points: Learning rate strongly affects optimization dynamics
common_wrong_ideas: Larger learning rates always converge faster
Smaller learning rates always converge to better minima
Learning rate only matters for SGD, not full-batch GD
